methodClasses.claimBoundary: Evaluates only explicit local numeric policy terms from admitted proposal/site facts; does not decide overall policy compliance or planning permission.
Character, layout, massing, amenity and context response remain planning/architectural judgement supported by evidence.
Flood/drainage/highway/parking evidence required by local planning policy remains external evidence and planning assessment; this class does not replace specialist technical design.
Planning permission, refusal, appeal and condition discharge remain external authority outcomes.

obligations.title: High-quality design respecting development pattern, scale, massing, appearance and local character
requiredInputs: evidenced local character / surrounding built and natural features
obligations.nonClaim: The two-house appeal's character harm is proposal-specific evidence and is not converted into a site-level fail or a universal dimensional rule.

obligations.title: Minimum private amenity-space quantity plus functional-quality duties
requiredInputs: qualifying private amenity area after local-policy exclusions
balcony dimensions where a balcony is relied upon
obligations.deterministicRule: minimum private amenity area = 5m2 for 1-2 occupants + 1m2 for each additional occupant; if a balcony is relied upon, minimum balcony width and depth = 1.5m
judgementRemainder: functional usability beyond the numeric minimum
correct exclusion of footpaths, driveways, front gardens, vehicle/cycle/refuse areas where applicable
obligations.compositionNote: This local obligation may overlap numerically with London Plan D6 but remains a separate local development-plan obligation with additional local exclusions / quality duties.

obligations.title: Host-property garden retention where development occurs in the grounds of an existing retained building
requiredInputs: whether the proposal is development in the grounds of an existing retained building
obligations.deterministicRule: retained host garden must have minimum length 10m and area no less than the smaller of one-half of the existing garden area or 200m2
obligations.nonClaim: DPL-RP-003 does not currently provide survey/title-grade host-garden geometry or legal parcel relationships sufficient to run this rule.

obligations.title: Protect neighbouring amenity, privacy, sunlight/daylight and functional private-space relationships
obligations.boundedPolicyFact: DM10.6(c) identifies direct overlooking of private outdoor space within 10m perpendicular to the rear elevation of a dwelling, but the complete DM10.6 assessment remains wider than one distance check.

obligations.title: Local flood-risk and sustainable-drainage planning duties
requiredInputs: authoritative flood-risk evidence from applicable sources
policyFacts: DM25.3 states sustainable drainage systems are required in all development
surface run-off should be managed as close to source as possible
drainage should accord with the London Plan sustainable-drainage hierarchy
obligations.nonClaim: Local planning drainage policy does not replace Part H, hydraulic design, LLFA evidence or environmental/sewer authority.

obligations.title: Sustainable travel, highway safety and severe-network-impact duties
requiredInputs: transport evidence proportionate to development scale

obligations.title: Local car/cycle-parking quality, safety and local requirements
requiredInputs: current London strategic parking-standard target applicable to the proposal
PTAL / on-street parking-stress evidence where relevant
obligations.compositionNote: The adopted local policy expressly refers to pan-London parking standards. DPL-10C does not hard-code superseded 2018-era London Plan table values as the current strategic target; current London strategic authority must be composed separately.

excludedOrHeldSources.reason: Woodside place context does not by itself prove DM47's named Portland Road spatial clauses apply to DPL-RP-003. Spatial applicability must come from the policy text / policies map, not the word 'Woodside'.

composition.rule: Local and strategic obligations coexist as typed development-plan authority. No precedence is inferred from list order or locality. Apparent conflict requires the planning/legal conflict semantics defined by DPL-10A rather than a more-local-wins rule.
composition.duplicateNumericPolicyRule: Where local and strategic policies express similar numeric requirements, preserve both obligation identities and their distinct additional conditions; do not merge them merely because the numeric baseline happens to match.
